sanskrit: āgataṃ no mitrabalaṃ praharadhvam abhītavat śabdavanto 'nudhāveyuḥ kurvanto bhairavaṃ ravam
english: "Our ally's host has come—strike, and have no fear!" Raising a fearsome din, they should rush forward with their war-cries.

sanskrit: kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāḥ śaṅkhāḥ krakacā goviṣāṇikān bherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavān nādayeyuś ca kuñjarān
english: Let them sound their roars and shrill cries, their conches, krakaca-rattles and cow-horns, their kettledrums, tabors and small drums—and make the war-elephants trumpet.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃśīlāḥ kiṃsamutthānāḥ kathaṃrūpāś ca bhārata kiṃsaṃnāhāḥ kathaṃśastrā janāḥ syuḥ saṃyuge nṛpa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what character, O Bhārata, of what bearing and of what aspect, what armor and what weapons should the men be who are to stand in battle, O king?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yathācaritam evātra śastrapatraṃ vidhīyate ācārād eva puruṣas tathā karmasu vartate
english: Bhīṣma said: A man's weapon and his armor are assigned here according to his custom, for it is according to his upbringing that a man conducts himself in his deeds.

sanskrit: gāndhārāḥ sindhusauvīrā nakharaprāsayodhinaḥ ābhīravaḥ subalinas tadbalaṃ sarvapāragam
english: The Gāndhāras, the Sindhus and the Sauvīras fight with claw-blades and lances; the Ābhīras are very strong, and their force is one that prevails everywhere.

sanskrit: sarvaśastreṣu kuśalāḥ sattvavanto hy uśīnarāḥ prācyā mātaṅgayuddheṣu kuśalāḥ śaṭhayodhinaḥ
english: The Uśīnaras are skilled in every weapon and full of mettle; the men of the east are skilled in elephant-warfare, though they fight by guile.

sanskrit: tathā yavanakāmbojā mathurām abhitaś ca ye ete niyuddhakuśalā dākṣiṇātyāsicarmiṇaḥ
english: So too the Yavanas and the Kāmbojas, and those who dwell about Mathurā, are skilled in close combat; the southerners are men of sword and shield.

sanskrit: sarvatra śūrā jāyante mahāsattvā mahābalāḥ prāya eṣa samuddiṣṭo lakṣaṇāni tu me śṛṇu
english: Heroes of great spirit and great strength are born everywhere. This much has been told in the main; now hear from me the marks of a warrior.

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlavāṅnetrāḥ siṃhaśārdūlagāminaḥ pārāvatakuliṅgākṣāḥ sarve śūrāḥ pramāthinaḥ
english: Those whose voice and eyes are like a lion's or a tiger's, whose gait is like a lion's or a tiger's, whose eyes are like a dove's or a sparrow's—all such are heroes, crushers of their foes.

sanskrit: mṛgasvarā dvīpinetrā ṛṣabhākṣās tathāpare pravādinaḥ sucaṇḍāś ca krodhinaḥ kiṃnarīsvanāḥ
english: Others with a wild beast's voice and a leopard's eyes, with a bull's eyes, loud of speech, exceedingly fierce, wrathful, with a voice like a kiṃnarī's—

sanskrit: meghasvanāḥ kruddhamukhāḥ ke cit karabhanisvanāḥ jihmanāsānujaṅghāś ca dūragā dūrapātinaḥ
english: some with a voice like thunder and an angry face, some with a young-camel's bellow; with crooked noses and slender shanks, who range far and strike at a distance—

sanskrit: biḍālakubjās tanavas tanukeśās tanutvacaḥ śūrāś capalacittāś ca te bhavanti durāsadāḥ
english: hunched like a cat, lean, with thin hair and thin skin, brave and restless of mind—such men prove hard to withstand.

sanskrit: godhānimīlitāḥ ke cin mṛduprakṛtayo 'pi ca turaṃgagatinirghoṣās te narāḥ pārayiṣṇavaḥ
english: Some whose eyes are half-closed like an iguana's, and mild by nature, who in motion sound like the tramp of horses—these men are capable of carrying a thing through.

sanskrit: susaṃhatāḥ pratanavo vyūḍhoraskāḥ susaṃsthitāḥ pravāditena nṛtyanti hṛṣyanti kalaheṣu ca
english: Well-knit, slender, broad-chested and well-formed, they dance when the drums sound and rejoice in quarrels.

sanskrit: gambhīrākṣā niḥsṛtākṣāḥ piṅgalā bhrukuṭīmukhāḥ nakulākṣās tathā caiva sarve śūrās tanutyajaḥ
english: Deep-eyed or with protruding eyes, tawny-hued, knit-browed of face, or with eyes like a mongoose's—all such are heroes ready to give up their bodies.

sanskrit: jihmākṣāḥ pralalāṭāś ca nirmāṃsahanavo 'pi ca vakrabāhvaṅgulīsaktāḥ kṛśā dhamanisaṃtatāḥ
english: Squint-eyed, with jutting foreheads, with fleshless jaws, with crooked arms and clenched fingers, gaunt and laced over with veins—

sanskrit: praviśanty ativegena saṃparāye 'bhyupasthite vāraṇā iva saṃmattās te bhavanti durāsadāḥ
english: when the clash is at hand they plunge in with great speed; like elephants in rut they prove hard to withstand.

sanskrit: dīptasphuṭitakeśāntāḥ sthūlapārśvahanūmukhāḥ unnatāṃsāḥ pṛthugrīvā vikaṭāḥ sthūlapiṇḍikāḥ
english: With blazing, bristling hair, with thick flanks, jaws and faces, with high shoulders and broad necks, grim of look and with thick calves—

sanskrit: udvṛttāś caiva sugrīvā vinatā vihagā iva piṇḍaśīrṣāhivaktrāś ca vṛṣadaṃśamukhā iva
english: with prominent eyes yet handsome necks, and stooped like birds; round-headed, with a serpent's mouth, or faces like a cat's—

sanskrit: ugrasvanā manyumanto yuddheṣv ārāvasāriṇaḥ adharmajñāvaliptāś ca ghorā raudrapradarśinaḥ
english: fierce-voiced, full of fury, who go forward in battle with a roar, ignorant of dharma and arrogant, dreadful and terrible to behold—

sanskrit: tyaktātmānaḥ sarva ete antyajā hy anivartinaḥ puraskāryāḥ sadā sainye hanyante ghnanti cāpi te
english: all these, careless of their lives, lowborn and never turning back, should always be set in the van of the army: they are slain, and they slay.

sanskrit: adhārmikā bhinnavṛttāḥ sādhv evaiṣāṃ parābhavaḥ evam eva prakupyanti rājño 'py ete hy abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
english: Lawless and of broken conduct, their ruin is itself a good thing; for in just this way they rise up again and again in rage even against their own king.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca jaitryā vā kāni rūpāṇi bhavanti puruṣarṣabha pṛtanāyāḥ praśastāni tānīhecchāmi veditum
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What, O bull among men, are the auspicious signs of an army destined to win victory? These I wish to learn here.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca jaitryā vā yāni rūpāṇi bhavanti puruṣarṣabha pṛtanāyāḥ praśastāni tāni vakṣyāmi sarvaśaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: The auspicious signs that mark an army destined to win victory, O bull among men, all of these I shall tell you in full.

sanskrit: daivaṃ pūrvaṃ vikurute mānuṣe kālacodite tad vidvāṃso 'nupaśyanti jñānadīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā
english: When the appointed time has summoned a human venture, fate first sets to work upon it; this the wise perceive with the far-reaching eye of knowledge.

sanskrit: prāyaścittavidhiṃ cātra japahomāṃś ca tadvidaḥ maṅgalāni ca kurvantaḥ śamayanty ahitāny api
english: And those who know such things, performing here the rites of expiation, their mutterings and oblations and acts of blessing, lay to rest even the ill-omened.

sanskrit: udīrṇamanaso yodhā vāhanāni ca bhārata yasyāṃ bhavanti senāyāṃ dhruvaṃ tasyāṃ jayaṃ vadet
english: The army in which the warriors and the mounts alike are high of heart—of that army, O Bhārata, one may surely foretell victory.

sanskrit: anv enāṃ vāyavo vānti tathaivendradhanūṃṣi ca anuplavante meghāś ca tathādityasya raśmayaḥ
english: When the winds blow at its back, and the rainbows of Indra, and the clouds and the sun's rays follow behind it—

sanskrit: gomāyavaś cānulomā vaḍā gṛdhrāś ca sarvaśaḥ ācareyur yadā senāṃ tadā siddhir anuttamā
english: and when jackals, crows and vultures move along with the host on the favorable side, then its success is unsurpassed.

sanskrit: prasannabhāḥ pāvaka ūrdhvaraśmiḥ; pradakṣiṇāvartaśikho vidhūmaḥ puṇyā gandhāś cāhutīnāṃ pravānti; jayasyaitad bhāvino rūpam āhuḥ
english: When the sacred fire is bright of flame, its rays mounting upward, its tongue curling to the right and free of smoke, and the holy fragrances of the oblations waft abroad—this, they say, is the sign of victory to come.

sanskrit: gambhīraśabdāś ca mahāsvanāś ca; śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca nadanti yatra yuyutsavaś cāpratīpā bhavanti; jayasyaitad bhāvino rūpam āhuḥ
english: Where the conches and kettledrums sound deep and resounding, and where the men are eager to fight and not set against it—this, they say, is the sign of victory to come.

sanskrit: iṣṭā mṛgāḥ pṛṣṭhato vāmataś ca; saṃprasthitānāṃ ca gamiṣyatāṃ ca jighāṃsatāṃ dakṣiṇāḥ siddhim āhur; ye tv agratas te pratiṣedhayanti
english: For those who have set out or are about to set out, deer behind and on the left are auspicious; for those who mean to strike, deer on the right betoken success; but those that cross in front forbid it.

sanskrit: maṅgalyaśabdāḥ śakunā vadanti; haṃsāḥ krauñcāḥ śatapatrāś ca cāṣāḥ hṛṣṭā yodhāḥ sattvavanto bhavanti; jayasyaitad bhāvino rūpam āhuḥ
english: When the birds cry with auspicious voices—geese, curlews, woodpeckers and blue jays—and the warriors are glad and full of spirit—this, they say, is the sign of victory to come.

sanskrit: śastraiḥ patraiḥ kavacaiḥ ketubhiś ca; subhānubhir mukhavarṇaiś ca yūnām bhrājiṣmatī duṣpratiprekṣaṇīyā; yeṣāṃ camūs te 'bhibhavanti śatrūn
english: Those whose host is radiant and hard to look upon for the bright gleam of weapons, armor, banners and standards and for the fair faces and the bright complexions of its young men—they overcome their enemies.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣavaś cānabhimāninaś ca; parasparaṃ sauhṛdam āsthitāś ca yeṣāṃ yodhāḥ śaucam anuṣṭhitāś ca; jayasyaitad bhāvino rūpam āhuḥ
english: Those whose warriors are obedient and free of vanity, who hold to friendship with one another and keep themselves pure—this, they say, is the sign of victory to come.

sanskrit: śabdāḥ sparśās tathā gandhā vicaranti manaḥpriyāḥ dhairyaṃ cāviśate yodhān vijayasya mukhaṃ tu tat
english: When the sounds, the touches and the scents that move about are pleasing to the mind, and firmness enters into the warriors—that is the face of victory.

sanskrit: iṣṭo vāmaḥ praviṣṭasya dakṣiṇaḥ pravivikṣataḥ paścāt saṃsādhayaty arthaṃ purastāt pratiṣedhati
english: For one who has entered, the omen on the left is favorable; for one about to enter, the right; an omen behind accomplishes the aim, while one in front forbids it.

sanskrit: saṃbhṛtya mahatīṃ senāṃ caturaṅgāṃ yudhiṣṭhira sāmnaivāvartane pūrvaṃ prayatethās tatho yudhi
english: Having gathered a great army of the four arms, O Yudhiṣṭhira, you should first strive to turn the foe back by conciliation, and only then by war.

sanskrit: jaghanya eṣa vijayo yad yuddhaṃ nāma bhārata yādṛcchiko yudhi jayo daivo veti vicāraṇam
english: This victory which is won by war is the lowest kind, O Bhārata, for in battle victory is a doubtful thing—whether it comes by chance or by fate is a matter of question.

sanskrit: apām iva mahāvegas trastā mṛgagaṇā iva durnivāryatamā caiva prabhagnā mahatī camūḥ
english: Like the great rush of waters, like herds of deer in panic, a great host once broken is most impossible to check.

sanskrit: bhagnā ity eva bhajyante vidvāṃso 'pi nakāraṇam udārasārā mahatī rurusaṃghopamā camūḥ
english: At the mere cry "It is broken!" even the wise break apart for no cause—a great host of noble strength, like a herd of ruru-deer.

sanskrit: parasparajñāḥ saṃhṛṣṭās tyaktaprāṇāḥ suniścitāḥ api pañcāśatiḥ śūrā mṛdnanti paravāhinīm
english: Heroes who know one another, joyful, careless of their lives and resolute—even fifty such can crush the army of the foe.

sanskrit: atha vā pañca ṣaṭ sapta sahitāḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ kulīnāḥ pūjitāḥ samyag vijayantīha śātravān
english: Or even five, six, or seven, joined together and firm of resolve, wellborn and rightly honored, will conquer their enemies here.

sanskrit: saṃnipāto na gantavyaḥ śakye sati kathaṃ cana sāntvabhedapradānānāṃ yuddham uttaram ucyate
english: Pitched battle should by no means be entered upon while another way is possible; war is said to be the last resort after conciliation, sowing dissension, and gifts.

sanskrit: saṃsarpaṇād dhi senāyā bhayaṃ bhīrūn prabādhate vajrād iva prajvalitād iyaṃ kva nu patiṣyati
english: For at the advance of an army fear afflicts the timid: "Where, like a blazing thunderbolt, will this thing fall?"

sanskrit: abhiprayātāṃ samitiṃ jñātvā ye pratiyānty atha teṣāṃ spandanti gātrāṇi yodhānāṃ viṣayasya ca
english: When men learn that a host has marched forth and go out to meet it, the limbs of the warriors quiver, and so does the whole country.

sanskrit: viṣayo vyathate rājan sarvaḥ sasthāṇujaṅgamaḥ śastrapratāpataptānāṃ majjā sīdati dehinām
english: The whole land is shaken, O king, with all that stands and moves within it; the very marrow sinks in the bodies of men scorched by the heat of arms.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sāntvaṃ krūramiśraṃ praṇetavyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ saṃpīḍyamānā hi pare yogam āyānti sarvaśaḥ
english: To them conciliation, mixed with sternness, should be applied again and again; for when hard pressed, the enemy will come round to terms in every way.

sanskrit: antarāṇāṃ ca bhedārthaṃ cārān abhyavacārayet yaś ca tasmāt paro rājā tena saṃdhiḥ praśasyate
english: To divide those within the enemy's ranks one should send forth spies; and with the king who lies beyond him, a treaty is to be commended.

sanskrit: na hi tasyānyathā pīḍā śakyā kartuṃ tathāvidhā yathā sārdham amitreṇa sarvataḥ pratibādhanam
english: For no other pressure of such a kind can be brought upon him as the assault from every side made together with his own enemy.

sanskrit: kṣamā vai sādhumāyā hi na hi sādhv akṣamā sadā kṣamāyāś cākṣamāyāś ca viddhi pārtha prayojanam
english: Forbearance is indeed a good thing, and impatience is never good; yet know, O Pārtha, the proper use of both forbearance and its opposite.

sanskrit: vijitya kṣamamāṇasya yaśo rājño 'bhivardhate mahāparādhā hy apy asmin viśvasanti hi śatravaḥ
english: The fame of a king who, having conquered, shows forbearance grows great, for then even those who have gravely offended come to trust in him.

sanskrit: manyate karśayitvā tu kṣamā sādhv iti śambaraḥ asaṃtaptaṃ tu yad dāru pratyeti prakṛtiṃ punaḥ
english: Śambara held that forbearance is good only after one has first worn the foe down; for wood that has not been heated returns again to its natural shape.

sanskrit: naitat praśaṃsanty ācāryā na ca sādhu nidarśanam akleśenāvināśena niyantavyāḥ svaputravat
english: This the teachers do not commend, nor is it a good example; rather, men should be governed without harshness and without destruction, as one would govern one's own son.

sanskrit: dveṣyo bhavati bhūtānām ugro rājā yudhiṣṭhira mṛdum apy avamanyante tasmād ubhayabhāg bhavet
english: A harsh king becomes hateful to all creatures, O Yudhiṣṭhira, yet a mild one men despise; therefore he should partake of both.

sanskrit: prahariṣyan priyaṃ brūyāt praharann api bhārata prahṛtya ca kṛpāyeta śocann iva rudann iva
english: When about to strike, he should speak kindly, and kindly too while striking, O Bhārata; and having struck, he should show pity, as one grieving, as one in tears.

sanskrit: na me priyaṃ yat sa hataḥ saṃprāhaivaṃ puro vacaḥ na cakartha ca me vākyam ucyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "It gives me no pleasure that he was slain"—thus he should say openly before others—"yet you did not heed my word though I told you again and again."

sanskrit: aho jīvitam ākāṅkṣe nedṛśo vadham arhati sudurlabhāḥ supuruṣāḥ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ
english: "Alas, how I longed that he should live! A man like this did not deserve to die. Hard indeed to find are good men who do not flee from battles."

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ mamāpriyaṃ tena yenāyaṃ nihato mṛdhe iti vācā vadan hantṝn pūjayeta rahogataḥ
english: "He who slew this man in the fray has done me a hurt"—saying this aloud, in secret he should yet honor the slayers.

sanskrit: hantṝṇāṃ cāhatānāṃ ca yat kuryur aparādhinaḥ krośed bāhuṃ pragṛhyāpi cikīrṣañ janasaṃgraham
english: And whatever wrong the slayers or those struck down may have done, he may even cry out with arms uplifted, wishing to win the people to himself.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvāsv avasthāsu sāntvapūrvaṃ samācaran priyo bhavati bhūtānāṃ dharmajño vītabhīr nṛpaḥ
english: Thus acting in all conditions with conciliation foremost, the king who knows dharma and is free of fear becomes dear to all creatures.

sanskrit: viśvāsaṃ cātra gacchanti sarvabhūtāni bhārata viśvastaḥ śakyate bhoktuṃ yathākāmam upasthitaḥ
english: And in him all creatures come to place their trust, O Bhārata; and one who is trusted, and so attended upon, can be enjoyed at will.

sanskrit: tasmād viśvāsayed rājā sarvabhūtāny amāyayā sarvataḥ parirakṣec ca yo mahīṃ bhoktum icchati
english: Therefore the king who wishes to enjoy the earth should win the trust of all creatures without guile, and guard them on every side.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ mṛdau kathaṃ tīkṣṇe mahāpakṣe ca pārthiva arau varteta nṛpatis tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How should a king conduct himself toward an enemy who is mild, how toward one who is fierce, and how toward one with a great following, O lord of the earth? Tell me that, grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bṛhaspateś ca saṃvādam indrasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue of Bṛhaspati and Indra, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiṃ devapatir abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ upasaṃgamya papraccha vāsavaḥ paravīrahā
english: Saluting Bṛhaspati and approaching him with joined palms, Vāsava, lord of the gods and slayer of enemy heroes, put this question to him:

sanskrit: ahiteṣu kathaṃ brahman vartayeyam atandritaḥ asamucchidya caivenān niyaccheyam upāyataḥ
english: "How, O holy one, should I bear myself toward my foes, ever vigilant, and how, without wholly destroying them, may I yet restrain them by stratagem?

sanskrit: senayor vyatiṣaṅgeṇa jayaḥ sādhāraṇo bhavet kiṃ kurvāṇaṃ na māṃ jahyāj jvalitā śrīḥ pratāpinī
english: "At the clashing of two armies victory is shared in common; doing what may I keep my blazing, glorious fortune from forsaking me?"

sanskrit: tato dharmārthakāmānāṃ kuśalaḥ pratibhānavān rājadharmavidhānajñaḥ pratyuvāca puraṃdaram
english: Then he who was skilled in dharma, profit and desire, ready of wit and learned in the ordinances of kingly duty, answered Puraṃdara:

sanskrit: na jātu kalahenecchen niyantum apakāriṇaḥ bālasaṃsevitaṃ hy etad yad amarṣo yad akṣamā na śatrur vivṛtaḥ kāryo vadham asyābhikāṅkṣatā
english: "Never should one seek to restrain wrongdoers by open strife, for fury and impatience are the resort of fools; nor should one openly show himself an enemy if one means his death.

sanskrit: krodhaṃ balam amarṣaṃ ca niyamyātmajam ātmani amitram upaseveta viśvastavad aviśvasan
english: "Curbing within himself the anger, the force and the impatience born of his own nature, he should wait upon his enemy as though trusting him, while trusting him not at all.

sanskrit: priyam eva vaden nityaṃ nāpriyaṃ kiṃ cid ācaret viramec chuṣkavairebhyaḥ kaṇṭhāyāsaṃ ca varjayet
english: "He should always speak kindly and do nothing unkind; he should desist from barren feuds and spare himself empty straining of the throat.

sanskrit: yathā vaitaṃsiko yukto dvijānāṃ sadṛśasvanaḥ tān dvijān kurute vaśyāṃs tathā yukto mahīpatiḥ vaśaṃ copanayec chatrūn nihanyāc ca puraṃdara
english: "As a skilled fowler, mimicking the cry of the birds, brings those birds under his power, so let the skilled king bring his enemies under his sway and then destroy them, O Puraṃdara.

sanskrit: na nityaṃ paribhūyārīn sukhaṃ svapiti vāsava jāgarty eva ca duṣṭātmā saṃkare 'gnir ivotthitaḥ
english: "One who forever scorns his foes does not sleep at ease, O Vāsava; the evil-minded man stays wakeful, like fire risen amid a heap of fuel.

sanskrit: na saṃnipātaḥ kartavyaḥ sāmānye vijaye sati viśvāsyaivopasaṃnyāsyo vaśe kṛtvā ripuḥ prabho
english: "No pitched battle should be joined when victory is doubtful; rather, the enemy, once trusted and won, should be brought under control and so disposed of, O lord.

sanskrit: saṃpradhārya sahāmātyair mantravidbhir mahātmabhiḥ upekṣamāṇo 'vajñāte hṛdayenāparājitaḥ
english: "Having taken counsel with his great-souled ministers versed in policy, he should look on as if indifferent though he be despised, unconquered in his heart;

sanskrit: athāsya praharet kāle kiṃ cid vicalite pade daṇḍaṃ ca dūṣayed asya puruṣair āptakāribhiḥ
english: "and then, when the time comes and his foe's footing has somewhat faltered, he should strike, and corrupt his army through trusted agents.

sanskrit: ādimadhyāvasānajñaḥ pracchannaṃ ca vicārayet balāni dūṣayed asya jānaṃś caiva pramāṇataḥ
english: "Knowing the beginning, middle and end, he should plot in secret, and corrupt his enemy's forces, having learned their full measure.

sanskrit: bhedenopapradānena saṃsṛjann auṣadhais tathā na tv eva celasaṃsargaṃ racayed aribhiḥ saha
english: "By sowing dissension, by bribes, and by employing drugs as well; but he should never enter into close fellowship with his foes.

sanskrit: dīrghakālam api kṣāntvā vihanyād eva śātravān kālākāṅkṣī yāmayec ca yathā visrambham āpnuyuḥ
english: "Though he must wait even a long while, biding his time, he should yet destroy his enemies; and he should keep them in check until they come to trust him."
